MFO — R package for Maximal Fat Oxidation and kinetics

Source: CLAUDE.md

What this repo is

R package MFO (CRAN: v0.1.0, 2022; GitHub: v0.2.0, Feb 2026). Computes maximal fat oxidation (MFO), Fatmax, Fatmax zone, crossover point and the SIN kinetics model (Chenevière 2009) from indirect-calorimetry data. Target users: sport and health scientists. Roadmap: v0.2.x on CRAN -> v0.3.0 (reliability, uncertainty, protocols, importers, Shiny app) -> JOSS paper.

The scientific specification lives in docs/SPEC.md (exported from the project doc “MFO: fundamentos científicos y técnicos”). Sections 9.5 and 12–17 are the backlog. Read SPEC.md before touching any formula. Never change a coefficient without citing the source in the roxygen block and adding a unit test against the paper’s numbers.

Working rules

  • Language: code, roxygen, NEWS, vignettes, commit messages in English. Conversation with Jorge in Spanish.
  • Jorge decides product/domain questions (what the user sees, which default, which reference population). Claude decides architecture and explains each decision in one line.
  • Be didactic: when introducing an R-package concept (roxygen tags, testthat edition 3, S3 classes, Suggests vs Imports, pkgdown, GitHub Actions) explain the why briefly.
  • Small commits, one topic each; conventional prefixes (feat:, fix:, docs:, test:, ci:, chore:). Every scientific change references a SPEC.md section in the body.
  • Never rewrite git history. Public history is a JOSS requirement.
  • Backwards compatibility: MFO(), MFO_kinetics(), MFOs() keep their arguments. New behaviour enters via new arguments with defaults or new functions.
  • Heavy optional deps (brms, rstan/cmdstanr, importer helpers) go in Suggests with requireNamespace() guards. Core must install in seconds.

Definition of done (every PR)

  • devtools::document() run; R CMD check --as-cran 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes (document any unavoidable NOTE in cran-comments.md).
  • devtools::test() green; new code covered; covr not lower than before.
  • NEWS.md entry under the unreleased heading.
  • If a formula or default changed: vignette and SPEC.md cross-reference updated.

Phase 1 backlog (v0.2.1 -> CRAN) — in order

  1. ci: GitHub Actions R-CMD-check (ubuntu/macos/windows) + test-coverage + pkgdown. Remove the dead Travis badge; add check/coverage/CRAN badges.
  2. docs: rewrite README for v0.2.x (methods P3/P2/MRER, equations, RER cutoff, relative outputs); fill NEWS.md (0.1.0, 0.2.0, 0.2.1).
  3. fix: VO2max from db_graded = highest rolling mean over vo2max_window s (default 30), not instantaneous max. SPEC 9.5 / 14.
  4. fix: basal substrate oxidation uses the same author equation as the test. SPEC 9.5.
  5. feat: include_basal = TRUE argument (basal point as step 0 in the fit). SPEC 9.5.
  6. fix: Jeukendrup–Wallis equations warn outside 40–75 %VO2max. SPEC 3 / 9.5.
  7. fix: SIN model formula: code has (pi^(1/s) / pi + 2*d); Chenevière 2009 eq. [14] is pi^(1/s) / (pi + 2*d). Add regression test with d = 0.18, s = 1.52, t = 0.21 (their Fig. 5): fitted curve must reproduce Fatmax = [(pi+2d)*2^(-1/s) - d - t]/K and Fatmin = (pi+d-t)/K. SPEC 6.5 / 19 (finding 5). 7b. fix: SIN fitting procedure: drop the P3 smoothing and synthetic grid; fit nlsLM directly to the observed step values (%MFO, normalised to observed max). Fatmin = second zero of the curve (default), fatmin_threshold optional. SPEC 19 (findings 3, 7). 7c. feat: method MV (measured values, with the author equation) and a real MRER (linear fits of (1-RER) and VO2 vs intensity, vertex of their product). Current MRER behaviour becomes MV; keep MRER string working with a deprecation message for one release. SPEC 6.1 / 19 (finding 4). 7d. fix: Rule: printed coefficient in the source > derived coefficient; derive only where the source prints no equation (SPEC 19). Péronnet–Massicotte print no equations, so use coefficients derived in code from their Table 1 constants (O2 0.7455 / CO2 0.7426 L per g glucose; 2.0092 / 1.4136 L per g fatty acid) with .derive_oxidation_coefficients(), the derivation explained in roxygen; unit test: 4.58519/3.22597 and 1.69469/1.70130. Frayn prints his equations, so keep 4.55/3.21 and 1.67/1.67 as printed; the derivation from his Table 1 is only a cross-check test. SPEC 19 (finding 6). 7e. feat: energy_equivalents argument with per-equation defaults (Péronnet 3.8683/9.7460 kcal/g; Jeukendrup 3.95 (40–50 %) / 4.07 (50–75 %) CHO and 9.75 fat, J&W 2005 Table 5; Frayn: product decision pending, see SPEC 19 finding 1). RER_cutoff accepts named values “classic” 1.00, “safe” 0.95, “sedentary” 0.93, “trained” 0.90 (Amaro-Gahete 2019). SPEC 19 (findings 1, 2).
  8. feat: warn on incomplete last step and on missing HR; min_steps (default 6) warning; warning when Fatmax lands on the first or last step. SPEC 9.5 / 14.
  9. docs: vignette “From gas exchange to Fatmax” reproducing the README example and explaining every parameter. pkgdown site with reference grouped by workflow.
  10. chore: cran-comments.md, inst/CITATION, submit v0.2.1 to CRAN.

Phase 2 (v0.3.0) starts after CRAN acceptance: SPEC sections 12–17, one issue each.

Repo conventions

  • R/ one file per exported function + utils-*.R for helpers; internal helpers prefixed ..
  • Tests mirror R/ file names. Numerical tests use tolerances stated in a comment with the source of the expected value.
  • Example data: data/ (rda) for small tables; inst/extdata/ for raw analyzer exports.
  • Datasets and example files must be anonymised; no participant identifiers ever.
